instruction: Adjust VLC settings to ensure videos are paused by default when opened, instead of playing immediately.

metadata.explanation: This task is infeasible because verifying the auto-pause on file open behavior requires loading a video file and checking whether playback starts automatically or remains paused. This runtime playback state behavior cannot be reliably captured and verified programmatically in the OSWorld environment.

llm_judge_reasons: Task is correctly marked as infeasible - the instruction requires verifying behavioral state (whether VLC pauses on file open) rather than just configuration settings

Verification would require opening a video file and capturing playback state immediately after opening, which involves timing-dependent runtime behavior that cannot be reliably verified programmatically

While VLC preferences may contain settings for this behavior, the instruction explicitly asks to verify the actual behavior ('pause automatically when a video file is opened'), not just the configuration
The 'infeasible' evaluator is the appropriate choice for this task given the practical limitations of capturing transient playback state in an automated testing environment
